original_extraction.evidence_text:
All this means is, there needs to be a balance. Aim to find that balance over time. Don’t put
ridiculous expectations on yourself, deciding that you’re never going to act on self-defeating urges
ever again. Of course you will—you’re human. You’ll screw up again and again over the course of
your life. But remember: the instant you are aware of what you’re doing, you have a chance to do
something more effective. And over time you’ll get better and better at catching yourself earlier and
earlier.

---

While urge surfing can be very helpful, like any skill, it requires practice. (Look, you had to know
that was coming.) The best way to practise is to put yourself in a situation where you’re likely to
feel confronted by troublesome urges. But don’t choose just any challenging situation; choose one
that moves your life forward in a meaningful way.

---

During the next week, pick two or three difficult situations that naturally occur when you take your
life in a valued direction. These situations could be anything: getting some exercise, attending a
class, asking someone out on a date or attempting something new at work. Once you’re in those
situations, notice your urges, surf them and stay fully engaged in what you’re doing.

---

Of course, staying engaged in what you’re doing can be tricky, especially when the thinking self
starts mouthing off. That’s why in the following chapters we’re going to look at a process called
‘connection’, which is all about engaging in and connecting with our experience (rather than getting
caught up in our thoughts and feelings).

---

Connection builds on, and overlaps with, expansion and defusion. So if you’re still struggling with
thoughts and feelings, you’ll find that connection skills will help you.

---

But before we get to that, we need to pay a very brief visit back to those demons on the boat...
generation_rules: Practice urge surfing in challenging but meaningful situations that advance valued life directions; gradually improve awareness and response to urges over time; engage fully in present activities despite internal experiences.
pause_rules: Implied pauses when shifting focus from urges to connection with experience; pauses to reflect on awareness moments.
original_extraction.psychological_function: Enhancing awareness of urges and behaviors; promoting acceptance of human imperfection; improving ability to catch oneself earlier in maladaptive patterns; increasing psychological flexibility through connection, expansion, and defusion processes.
repetition_rules: Emphasize repeated practice of urge surfing and catching oneself earlier in maladaptive behaviors.
original_extraction.therapeutic_function: Developing skill in urge surfing to manage self-defeating urges and increase effective responses over time; fostering engagement in valued life directions despite challenging urges; building connection with present experience to reduce fusion with thoughts and feelings.
voice_rules: Use a balanced, non-judgmental tone acknowledging human imperfection; encourage gradual progress and self-compassion; prepare for upcoming introduction of connection skills.
